source.title: Learning hidden structures in open quantum dynamics

purpose: Test whether invariant observable-structure hypotheses can be identified from restricted multi-time measurements in known finite-dimensional open-system models, and measure total resources per accepted structure without inferring advantage from state-space size.

model_scope.incumbent_model: Finite-dimensional Markovian open-system model with declared generator and accessible observables.
model_scope.mathematical_check: For declared Heisenberg-picture generator L_dagger and candidate observable subspace A, test L_dagger(A) subseteq A; separately test linear-subspace and algebra closure. Decoherence-free labels require additional declared conditions and are not inferred from invariance alone.
model_scope.non_markovian_models: Negative-control / abstention arm; not silently fit as Markovian truth.

benchmark_arms: known decoherence-free structure with separately verified conditions

split_and_budget.held_out_unit: whole model family and parameter regime; no random row split alone

metrics: calibration and abstention rate on unidentifiable cases
measurement settings and shots per accepted structure
wall time and host CPU/GPU time
target/provider billable usage and energy where measurable

acceptance.rule: Freeze numerical thresholds before candidate generation; require held-out performance, exact/declared-tolerance mathematical checks, calibrated uncertainty, no hidden failures, and resource reporting. Any claimed decoherence-free structure must pass its separate mathematical conditions.

order: authorized real-QPU only after separate consent

non_claims: no readable classical memory/storage replacement from algebra or Hilbert-space dimension
no measured energy or cost reduction
next_gate: Implement exact small-model fixtures and a deterministic classical baseline, then run blind family-disjoint tests and adversarial negative controls.
